description: We are college girls in STEM with a strong interest in astronomy, physics, data science, research, space exploration, technology, creativity and good communication who turn complex scientific concepts into practical project ideas. We welcome anyone who has a strong interest in learning outside the box, creating innovative designs with developed skills.
summary: Aztroteca is a search engine that identifies places on Earth with environmental conditions similar to those found on Mars, focusing exclusively on Mexico. While existing tools allow users to view environmental factors layer by layer, Aztroteca brings different variables together to find and compare potential Martian analog sites across the country. To our knowledge, there are no existing tools with this same focus on Mexico and this combination of variables. Our project aims to explore areas that have not received much attention and identify places that could be valuable for future research on Mars. Aztroteca also creates an opportunity to connect Mexican research with the international space community, encourage collaboration, and bring more attention to Mexico's role in space exploration. By making this information easier to explore, we hope to show the potential of Mexico's landscapes to contribute to the study of other planets.
details:
Aztroteca is a search engine for locations on Earth that are analogous to Martian environments. As a first step, we download public NASA databases, which we then clean and analyze using predefined variables and values. Our expected impact is to promote international collaboration and to raise the visibility of the space sector in Mexico.

To develop our product, we used Claude to address specific questions and debug our code. For database analysis, we relied on QGIS and Python, and we built the preliminar website with Vercel, although our ultimate version was produced with HTML. We also created a project demo using Genially.

Our project explores places in Mexico that have not been previously studied. Aztroteca is innovative because, although there are existing websites and applications that display various factors layer by layer, to our knowledge none of them focuses exclusively on Mexico as a study area, nor do they feature the specific combination of variables that we employ. The datasets we have compiled, which contain the variables and values we defined, are among the first to identify locations within Mexico that serve as analogs to Mars.

We have focused our analysis on Mexico not only because of our own identity, but also because we consider it a country exceptionally rich in geological and climatic diversity, making it an ideal candidate for finding Mars analogs.

This focus on Mexico is also the foundation of our visual identity. Our logo, drawn in AutoCAD, depicts an ear of corn shaped like a spaceship, a tribute to the cultural importance of corn in our country. We defined our color palette using Canva. The name Aztroteca is a wordplay combining “astro” and “azteca.”

We established aridity, vegetation index, dust, and daytime and nighttime thermal extremes as a preliminary filter. This filter allowed us to delineate zones meeting these general criteria, within which we then analyzed an additional 49 variables covering geology, topography, climate, temperature, illumination, atmosphere, wind, water, resources, biology, habitability, subsurface conditions, caves, and operational factors.

This first stage of the project is based on Mars data. In the next stage, we will analyze lunar data to identify analogs in Mexico, and in the third stage, we will extend the study area to the American continent.
